summary: AE + SE demo of Redwood Hosted API focusing on embeddings + reranking for SilverFin's search relevance use case. Covered architecture, API walkthrough for embeddings and rerank endpoints, demo of console logs/Optimize suggestions, security questions (SOC2/SAML/KMS), and next steps to run a small benchmark with 10k docs.
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Lee: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm jordan from Redwood Inference, i'm the AE on this account. quick intro, we've got priya our solutions engineer and marta on the line as well. how's everyone doing?
[00:07] Aisha Patel: good, thanks. excited to see the embeddings stuff. we've been trying to improve relevancy for product search, lots of long tail queries.
[00:15] Priya Desai: great, i'll lead the technical walkthrough — i'll show the hosted embeddings endpoint and the rerank flow that we typically recommend for search relevance. quick note: transcription might be a bit off for some product names, so i'll repeat key endpoints.
[00:25] Tom Ruiz: quick ask on the security side — we'll need SOC 2 details and SAML/SSO info, also KMS support for keys.
[00:33] Jordan Lee: yes we will share SOC 2 report and the security questionnaire, and we do have KMS integrations for private key management.
[00:40] Priya Desai: ok jumping in. main pattern we demo is two-step: 1) call the embeddings endpoint to vectorize documents and user queries, 2) run a dense retrieval followed by our rerank endpoint which takes the query, candidate doc texts, and returns a relevance-ordered list. code snippet coming up.
[00:55] [01:05] Priya Desai: (screen) here's the hosted API call for embeddings — POST /v1/embeddings with model param, supports batching. you can send up to 1k texts per request but typical sweet spot is 100-500 for latency. note that our embedding dims are configurable per model but commonly 1536 or 2048 depending on the model.
[01:25] Marcus Chen: is the batching server-side or do we group at client? we have a lambda-based uploader so curious about ideal grouping.
[01:30] Priya Desai: good q — batching is at the client first; the hosted endpoint accepts batch requests and our runtime does some continuous batching under the hood to improve throughput. for lambdas, we recommend grouping to ~200 items per request to keep latency predictable. there's also an autosized host-side batching but it's workload dependent.
[01:46] [02:10] Priya Desai: moving to rerank. POST /v1/rerank where you send query + top-k candidates (we support up to 50 candidates in a single request). rerank uses the model to score and reorder candidates; typical flows preselect top 100 via ANN and then rerank top 10-50 for best precision.
[02:30] Lena Wong: can you show the request payload? we have some structured fields like brand, category, availability — can those be included?
[02:36] Priya Desai: yes, you can include metadata as context fields. those get concatenated or provided as structured inputs depending on the model prompt template. we demo a template now where we include brand and in_stock flags to bias the rerank.
[02:54] [03:15] Priya Desai: (demo) here's a live rerank call — you can see latency ~120ms for a 10-candidate rerank on hosted. for 50 candidates latency goes up to ~250-300ms depending on model size. these numbers are representative on our hosted fleet in us-west.
[03:35] Tom Ruiz: that's promising. what's cost like? i know latency scales with candidates — any recommendations to reduce units?
[03:40] Priya Desai: yes, we recommend a two-stage approach: ANN/approximate search to cut to 50, then rerank top 10-20. also use prefix/KV cache for popular queries, and Redwood Optimize will suggest quantization/profile changes if you need lower token cost.
[03:56] Jordan Lee: to add, our Optimize tool can run on sample workloads and recommend batching, quantization, and caching to reduce per-query cost by 30-60% depending on traffic patterns.
[04:10] [04:25] Aisha Patel: about ANN — we're using OpenSearch + vectorembedding plugin currently; do you integrate with those or do we need to change infra?
[04:32] Priya Desai: we integrate easily — most customers keep their vector DB/ANN and call Redwood for rerank, or we can host embeddings and point them to your vector DB. common combos are OpenSearch, Pinecone, or Weaviate for ANN with Redwood doing the re-ranking and generation.
[04:50] Marcus Chen: are there SDKs? we prefer python/node.
[04:54] Priya Desai: yes SDKs for python, node, go; examples in the quickstart repo. i'll paste links after.
[05:03] [05:30] Priya Desai: switching to the console — here's the per-route dashboard, latency and token cost breakdown, and a rerank-specific trace that highlights token usage for candidate contexts. you can also pin model versions for canary rollouts.
[05:50] Lena Wong: can we see where Optimize surfaced suggestions?
[05:55] Marta Velez: sure — Optimize runs offline evaluations and shows a list: suggested batch size 256, enable quantization profile q4_8 for this model family, and enable per-customer prefix cache for recurring queries. it also computes expected cost savings and estimated latency impact.
[06:18] [06:40] Tom Ruiz: security — KMS + SAML. can you confirm keys never leave our KMS?
[06:46] Jordan Lee: yes for Private deployments keys can remain in your KMS/HSM. for hosted we offer customer-managed KMS in select plans; we'll document exact flow in the security packet.
[06:58] Aisha Patel: do you offer dedicated capacity if we need predictable p95 latency?
[07:04] Jordan Lee: yes, Redwood Dedicated is an option — dedicated GPU pools, autoscaling policies, and SLA-backed latency. we'll run a cost tradeoff exercise in the follow-up.
[07:15] [07:30] Priya Desai: back to rerank — one tip: provide a compact candidate context to reduce token count (truncate long docs to highlights). we also support structured feature inputs so you can train prompt templates that better use category/brand signals.
[07:45] Marcus Chen: curious about embeddings dimension — will we need vector DB changes if we switch model?
[07:50] Priya Desai: most vector DBs support different dims; however when switching model families it's best to reindex embeddings. Optimize can recommend which model/quant profile gives best tradeoff for your precision/cost needs.
[08:10] [08:40] Priya Desai: demo of a slightly imperfect transcript: sorry, that's me. moving on: here's a sample benchmark we run: ingest 10k documents, generate embeddings, run 5k queries, compute MRR/NDCG pre and post rerank. the benchmark spreadsheet shows per-query latency and per-candidate token usage.
[09:05] Aisha Patel: what's a typical improvement in NDCG?
[09:10] Priya Desai: customers see 10-30% improvement in NDCG when they add rerank on top of ANN, depending on query complexity and doc structure.
[09:20] [09:40] Jordan Lee: quick commercial note — hosted API pricing is usage based; we can open a trial with credits to run the benchmark. if predictability is a requirement we'll explore Dedicated and reserved capacity.
[09:55] Tom Ruiz: on data residency — we need EU-only hosting for some datasets.
[10:00] Marta Velez: we have region controls; hosted EU regions are available and Private deployments support fully on-prem. we'll add region notes in the follow-up packet.
[10:12] [10:35] Priya Desai: now walking through an example rerank request — (code) payload: {query: "noise cancelling headphones", candidates: [{id:1, text:"...",meta:{brand:"Aurora"}},...], features:{in_stock:true}}. response includes scores and explanation tokens if you enable debug mode. note debug increases token count.
[10:58] Lena Wong: is there an option to return explanations or rationales? we want traceability for ranking decisions.
[11:05] Priya Desai: yes, you can enable structured output and explanations — they show token-level highlights, though they add cost. another pattern is to sample a subset of queries for explanations and keep standard rerank for bulk traffic.
[11:25] [11:50] Jordan Lee: any blockers on your side to run a pilot?
[11:55] Aisha Patel: main blockers: security review, cost/time to reindex, and proving relevance improvements with our dataset.
[12:03] Jordan Lee: totally reasonable — we'll send the security packet and a benchmark template. priya will share the scripts.
[12:12] [12:30] Priya Desai: quick note on telemetry — the console shows token-level breakdown and route-level SLOs; you can set alerts when p95 crosses thresholds or when token usage per route spikes.
[12:45] Tom Ruiz: for integration, do we have a white-glove onboarding for the first pilot?
[12:50] Jordan Lee: yes, we offer solutions hours in the enterprise pack; for the pilot we can include one week of SE time to run the benchmark and tune rerank templates.
[13:05] [13:30] Marcus Chen: any gotchas around rate limits for the embeddings bulk upload?
[13:36] Priya Desai: we'll give a recommended throttle; for big backfills we often suggest a backfill token with a burst policy or use our bulk ingestion pipeline. we'll include that in the onboarding doc.
[13:50] Aisha Patel: what about compliance — do you provide logs for audits?
[13:56] Marta Velez: yes audit logs per tenant, access logs, and we keep model call traces for configured retention windows. retention can be adjusted per contract.
[14:10] [14:40] Jordan Lee: ok to recap quickly: we'll send pricing + trial creds; priya will send benchmark + scripts; aisha will share sample queries and doc subset; tom will confirm security recipients. schedule follow-up next week to go over Dedicated vs Hosted cost tradeoff.
[14:58] Lena Wong: thanks, this was useful.
[15:03] Jordan Lee: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the packet.
[15:10] [15:20] MEETING ENDS
notes: Customer is a mid-stage e-commerce search team focused on improving long-tail relevance. Main asks: security docs (SOC2/SAML/KMS), benchmark with 10k docs, cost comparison hosted vs dedicated. AE+SE present. Action items assigned.
